submission.rationale: This receiving fermentation shows a normal, healthy trajectory. Online DO2 observations through 52 h range ~8.8-14.8 mg/L with the latest value ≈ 10.97 mg/L — all far above the 2 mg/L hard limit. The mild DO dips (e.g., ~8.83 mg/L near t=122 h) mirror the same oscillatory pattern seen in all three source batches, which recover and continue to high DO, so this is expected process behavior, not an incipient oxygen failure. Delayed product assays show steady product growth (0.006 → 0.018 → 0.92 → 2.69 g/L at t=59,119,179,239), consistent with a productive run. The source-calibrated forward model for KEEP predicts a post-decision minimum DO of 8.17 mg/L (zero hours below limit, zero oxygen deficit) with terminal product mass ~576 kg at 6.88 g/L, and all 5 sensitivity members are feasible (min DO range 6.86-9.21 mg/L). Since KEEP is centrally feasible with a large margin (~4x the limit), any feed reduction or air increase would unnecessarily sacrifice product mass or add unmodeled operating risk. No intervention is justified; KEEP retains maximum product mass while meeting the DO constraint.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated and imperfect; source and receiving processes differ. However, the model margin is enormous (~8.2 mg/L predicted minimum vs the 2 mg/L limit) and even the most pessimistic sensitivity member (6.86 mg/L) stays far above the limit, while the direct receiving observations themselves (minimum ~8.8 mg/L over 52 h) independently corroborate feasibility. Residual risk would be an abrupt receiving-specific metabolic shift not present in the source history; the observed oscillatory DO pattern recovering repeatedly argues against this. Confidence in KEEP feasibility is high.
